summary: Shu-fen Chen works in linguistics and Indology. She studied at National Tsing Hua University under Chin-Fa Lien and completed doctoral studies under Hans Henrich Hock, later serving as a professor at National Tsing Hua University (attested 2010).

Shubhachandra is an Indologist who served as a professor at Karnatak University (attested 2001) and held a post in the Department of Jainology and Prakrits at the University of Mysore (attested 2002).
Shubhangni Gupta works in Indology, history, and archaeology. She pursued doctoral studies at Stanford University, where she was a PhD candidate in 2019.

Shuddhatam Prakash Jain works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, holding degrees from several institutions including CSU and JVBI. He taught at Central Sanskrit University, Mangalayatan University, Ghanaram Hariram College (professor 2014–2015), and Somaiya Vidyavihar University (2015).

Shudo Ishii is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University under Shigeo Kamata. He spent his career at Komazawa University from assistant in 1971 to professor by 1984, and served as acting head of Matsugaoka Bunko.

Shuhong Chang was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who studied in China and France. He taught at the Central Academy of Fine Arts and served as director and honorary director of the Dunhuang Academy.

Shuichi Kato was a scholar of Japanology, history, and philosophy who studied medicine at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at the University of British Columbia, Sophia University, and Ritsumeikan University, directing the Kyoto Museum for World Peace.
Shuichi Maida was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Kyoto University and was a student of Haya Akegarasu.

Shuichi Nara works in Indology and philosophy. Educated at Keio University, he has served as a full-time researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute and as a lecturer at Chuo University (attested 2026).

Shuji Takayama is a Buddhist studies scholar who held research and lecturer positions at Ryukoku University, Bukkyo University, Musashino University, and Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College between 2003 and 2006.
Shujiro Shimada was a scholar of Japanology, sinology, and art history who studied at Kyoto University (1928–1931) and held a post at Princeton University from circa 1962 to 1975.

Shujun Motegi is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi at Banaras Hindu University and earned an MA from Kyoto University. He served as Professor of Ethics at Shinshu University (attested 2010).

Shuken Ito is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his degrees, including a doctorate, at Komazawa University. He served at Komazawa University from research assistant in 1973 to professor in 1991, and was a visiting professor at Aichi Gakuin University.
Shuman Chen specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Chen studied under traditional teacher Weijue Shi and completed a PhD at Northwestern University under the supervision of Brook Ziporyn.

Shuming Liang was a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and Buddhist studies who attended Shuntian Middle School. He joined the philosophy department at Peking University in 1917 and later founded the Shandong Rural Reconstruction Institute and the China Democratic League.

Shumpei Ueyama was a scholar of philosophy, Japanology, and history who studied at Kyoto University. He served as professor at Kyoto University (1968), president of Kyoto City University of Arts (1989–1995), and director of Kyoto National Museum.
Shun Hidaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a researcher at the Buddhist Art Resource Center in 2012 and as a part-time lecturer at Otani University (attested 2014).

Shun'ei Hirai is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. He had a long academic career at Komazawa University, serving as professor, vice president (1986), and emeritus professor (2001).
Shun'ei Mori is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. He held posts at Ryukoku University (attested 1990) and Chikushi Jogakuen Junior College (attested 1995).
Shunei Tsuboi was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Bukkyo University (attested in 1963 and 1972).
